questions.solution:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in the Direct Speech whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No" in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions "if" or "whether".

For example:

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the simple present tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the simple past tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said to him' will be changed to 'enquired'.

'Whether' will be introduced in the sentence.

'Your' will be changed to 'his'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): He enquired whether his name was not Ahmed.

questions.question: Select the correct active form of the given sentence. AIDS will have been cured by the year 2070 by scientists.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

AIDS will have been cured by the year 2070 by scientists.

options.text: Scientists will have cured AIDS by the year 2070.
options.html: Scientists will have cured AIDS by the year 2070.

options.text: Scientists cured AIDS by the year 2070.
options.html: Scientists cured AIDS by the year 2070.

options.text: Scientists will cure AIDS by the year 2070.
options.html: Scientists will cure AIDS by the year 2070.

options.text: Scientists must have cured AIDS by the year 2070.
options.html: Scientists must have cured AIDS by the year 2070.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ('been' in the given sentence) and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Perfect. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case)

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

For example:

The gold will have been bought by her. (Passive Voice)

She will have bought the gold. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): Scientists will have cured AIDS by the year 2070.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'consensus' from the following sentence. The landowner and the tenant mutually came to an agreement for decisive acceptance of its clause.

questions.solution:
The given sentence is in simple past tense. So, the sentence in direct form should be in simple present tense.

Among the given options, options (b) and (d) are not in simple present tense forms. Option (c) is grammatically incorrect as we use 'do' with the pronoun 'you', and not 'does'.

So, the correct sentence is: Raveena asked me, "Do you have my maid's number?"

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution:
Serve - perform duties or services for (another person or an organization).

Drain - cause the water or other liquid in (something) to run out, leaving it empty or dry.

Lag - fail to keep up with another or others in movement or development.

Debit - (of a bank or other financial organization) remove (an amount of money) from a customer's account.

The sentence conveys the speaker's views that he/she will not take a certain action regarding something he/she does not even believe.

Filling the blank with 'serve' gives the meaning that the speaker does not want to perfume duties with respect to something they have no trust in.

Other options render the sentence meaningless.

So, option (a) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
Sometimes - occasionally, rather than all of the time.

Nevertheless - in spite of that; notwithstanding; all the same.

Whether - expressing a doubt or choice between alternatives.

Presumably - used to convey that what is asserted is very likely though not known for certain.

The clause with he blank is the continuation of the sentence which conveys that the speaker does not want to perfume duties with respect to something they have no trust in.

The clause after the blank lists the alternatives that can be the things that the author does not believe in (home, fatherland or church).

So, to represent these alternatives, we would use 'whether'.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.solution:
Express - convey (a thought or feeling) in words or by gestures and conduct.

Disappear - cease to be visible.

Collect - bring or gather together (a number of things).

Sterilise - make (something) free from bacteria or other living microorganisms.

Filling the blank with 'express' gives the meaning that the author wants to convey his/her thoughts through art. Other options render the sentence meaningless.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.solution:
Morbidly - in a way that is unusual and is regarded as disturbing or unhealthy.

Bleakly - ​in a way that does not give any reason to have hope or expect anything good.

Pithily - in a clever way that uses only a few words.

Freely - not under the control of another; as one wishes.

Wholly - entirely; fully

The given sentence conveys that the author wants to convey themselves as wholly as they can. The word in the blank should be in line with 'wholly' because the connector 'and' connects two things or people that are closely linked.

So, only 'freely' fits in the blank.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
Behave - act or conduct oneself in a specified way, especially towards others.

Allow - let (someone) have or do something.

Caution - say something as a warning.

Effeminate - An effeminate man behaves or looks similar to a woman.

The reflexive pronoun 'myself' will be used after the verb to denote that the object of the verb is the subject itself. So, option (d) is incorrect as it is a noun.

Filling the blank with 'allow' implies that the author talks about the methods that they would let them use. Other options render the sentence meaningless.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'. I have reached the hotel , by the time you call me.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

I have reached the hotel, by the time you call me.
questions.solution:
The sentence denotes the activity that had already taken place by the time the subject was called.

So, the action was done in the past which implies the usage of the present perfect tense is incorrect.

For the same reason, the usage of future tense as in options (a) and (c) is also incorrect.

The underlined segment can be correctly replaced with 'had reached the hotel'.

The correct sentence is: I had reached the hotel, by the time you call me.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. The prisoner was / accused for stealing / from his landlord.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The prisoner was / accused for stealing / from his landlord.
questions.solution:
The verb 'accused' is followed by 'of' and not 'for'. So, the part in option (a) has an error.

The correct sentence is: The prisoner was accused of stealing from his landlord.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence. Old people acquire experience through age.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Old people acquire experience through age.
questions.solution:
Acquire - buy or obtain (an asset or object) for oneself/ learn or develop (a skill, habit, or quality).

Gain - obtain or secure (something wanted or desirable)/ reach or arrive at (a destination).

As per the stated meanings, the verb 'gain' fits with 'experience'. 'Experience' is not an object or a skill, habit or quality that can be acquired.

It is the stage of person's involvement in a certain thing.

So, option (d) 'gain experience' can replace the underlined segment.

The correct sentence is: Old people gain experience through age.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Indefinite tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Indefinite.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. It is a very popular character and is the mascot for Walt Disney company. B. Mickey generally appears with his girlfriend Minnie Mouse and pet Pluto. C. The animated movies on Mickey mouse have been nominated for the Academy award. D. Mickey mouse is a fictional cartoon character created by Walt Disney in 1928.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It is a very popular character and is the mascot for Walt Disney company.

B. Mickey generally appears with his girlfriend Minnie Mouse and pet Pluto.

C. The animated movies on Mickey mouse have been nominated for the Academy award.

D. Mickey mouse is a fictional cartoon character created by Walt Disney in 1928.
questions.solution:
Sentence D comes first as it introduces the subject of discussion - 'Mickey Mouse'. Sentence A comes next and informs about its popularity. Sentence B comes next and gives further information (about other characters). Sentence C gives an update about the animated movies on Mickey mouse.

So, the correct order is DABC.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. P. There once was a little boy who had a very bad temper. Q. The boy gradually began to control his temper over the next few weeks, and the number of nails he was hammering into the fence slowly decreased. R. His father decided to hand him a bag of nails and said that every time the boy lost his temper, he had to hammer a nail into the fence. S. On the first day, the boy hammered 37 nails into that fence.
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P. There once was a little boy who had a very bad temper.

Q. The boy gradually began to control his temper over the next few weeks, and the number of nails he was hammering into the fence slowly decreased.

R. His father decided to hand him a bag of nails and said that every time the boy lost his temper, he had to hammer a nail into the fence.

S. On the first day, the boy hammered 37 nails into that fence.
questions.solution:
Sentence P comes first as it introduces the subject of the passage and a problem with him. How his father decided to deal with the problem is mentioned in sentence R, so it comes next. Sentences S and Q form the pair SQ as sentence S mentions the first day of implementation of father's solution, and sentence Q updates about the progress over the next few weeks.

So, the correct order is PRSQ.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.
